title: Rav Menashe bar Yirmeyah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Pesachim 28a and Nazir 65b for “Menashe bar Yirmeyah said in the name of Rav.” He also cites Bava Batra 146a [147a in the consulted text], where Rav Menashia bar Yirmeyah says, “From here,” and then Rami bar Yechezkel says, “From here.” Hyman infers that Menashe was a student of Rav.

Ohr Zarua, partII, supplied ספ״ד [a matching passage is at section84:1], cites “Chanan bar Immi said before Rav Yehudah in Menashe bar Yirmeyah’s name.” Hyman traces this to Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat6:5, where he says an error occurred: “Anan bar R’ Ima [supplied אנן בר׳ אימא] said before Rabbi Yehudah: Menashya bar Menashe Yirmeyah, provided…” Hyman says it SHOULD READ as cited in Ohr Zarua, and identifies him as Rav Menashya bar Yirmeyah, Rav’s student.

notes.text: Anan is a personal name, not the pronoun “we.” The supplied Menashya bar Menashe Yirmeyah chain remains malformed and is not quietly replaced; Hyman proposes Or Zarua’s shorter reading.

The whole saved Zhytomyr1862 Ohr Zarua II84:1 scalar has Chanan bar Immi before full Rav Yehudah in Menashe bar Yirmeyah’s name. The whole saved Guggenheimer Shabbat6:5 scalar instead has Anan כר׳ אימי, full Rabbi Yehudah, and Menashya bar Menashe Yirmeyah; supplied בר׳ אימא remains distinct. Anan is a personal name, not we. The older end-of-chapter4 rendering of ספ״ד is not verified: section84:1 supplies the actual matching text, while the supplied notation is retained. Hyman says the Yerushalmi SHOULD READ as Ohr Zarua and identifies Rav Menashya as Rav’s student; the force and ownership remain, without proving scribal history or merging homonyms. Uninspected abbreviated Ima remains R-prime. Pesachim/Nazir/BavaBatra citations are inherited, not newly inspected whole folios.

Hyman’s print (III, p. 895) cites Pesachim 28a and Bava Batra 146a. The consulted Nazir 65b names Rav Menashya bar Yirmeyah reporting Rav. The two consecutive proofs are in the consulted Bava Batra 147a. Menashya cites Hezekiah’s instruction to his household and Rami cites Ahithophel’s. No matching name was located in the bounded comparison of Pesachim 28a, 28b, 29a and 30a. The printed Ohr Zarua notation ספ״ד and the shorter chain attested at II 84:1 are distinct from the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:5 reading כר׳ אימי. Hyman proposes his correction on the strength of the Ohr Zarua quotation.
